T1.summary_unbriefed:
**Story: Reconstruction documentation (Serbia, from November 2024), status as of 2024-12-26**

**Background:** On 1 Nov 2024 the canopy at the Novi Sad railway station collapsed, killing 15 (two others seriously injured). The station was reconstructed in phases within the Belgrade–Budapest rail project with China and Hungary. Core dispute: who is responsible, and whether the canopy fell within the reconstruction documentation (CIP project documents of 15 Nov showed canopy work planned, contradicting Tica's "not in scope" claim of 1 Nov).

**Investigation/earlier events (condensed):** Novi Sad prosecution questioned 100+, about 10 detained (14 Dec); responsibility awaits expert analysis. Vesić resigned 4 Nov; arrests reported 22–28 Nov (opposition cites 12, calls them staged). Vučević (16 Dec) claims "13 people prosecuted"; charges not officially detailed. Subcontractor Starting's state contracts reported. 22 Nov: attack on FDU students and professors (students blamed local SNS representatives; not officially established); Belgrade Higher Public Prosecutor's Office took over the FDU dean's complaint against unknown persons (13 Dec). Opposition claims the station was used without a use permit (unverified). [person] (17 Dec) published a ministry decision showing Vesić delegated responsibility for 167 infrastructure projects; no legal assessment yet. Dašić (19 Dec): several top officials bear criminal responsibility (opinion, unverified). 21 Dec: commentator says ex-acting director of Infrastruktura železnice's statement suggests blame-shifting; statement not detailed. 24 Dec: commentary says prosecutor Zagorka Dolovac can inspect all documentation and issue binding instructions to prosecutors.

**Student blockade movement:** Open-ended blockades since 2 Dec; by 19 Dec at 62 faculties of five state universities, at least one private faculty, four vocational schools, plus several high schools. Demands: full documentation; criminal and political responsibility; prosecution of FDU attackers; dropping charges against detained/arrested students and young people; 20% more education funding. 22 Dec: mass Slavija gathering (Belgrade), described as Serbia's largest protest of the 21st century, peaceful. 23–24 Dec: "Zastani, Srbijo" silences and blockades in multiple cities; Niš, Leskovac, Kruševac, Valjevo developments; high-school collective says blockade continues past 20 Jan if demands unmet.

**New (25–26 Dec):**
- 25 Dec: Law Faculty students delivered ~1,000 letters to prosecutor Dolovac outside the Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office, urging her to "do her job" and start meeting demands (including confirmation of attackers' identities and dropping charges against arrested students/professors). Chanting "Meet the demands" and "No negotiations." Dolovac accepted the letter and invited students to talk; no meeting outcome reported.
- 25 Dec: N1 reports BIA (security agency) summoned a student for a "friendly talk" about faculty protests, reportedly the first such contact; unconfirmed beyond N1.
- 25 Dec: Vučić reportedly gathering his "youth" in Sava Centar as a counter to blockades; Đilas (SSP) disputes SNS support claims (says below 40%) and says Vučić can't publish all documentation because it would reveal corruption (opinion).
- Niš: university supports demands but opposes blockades of faculty work; students to block Most mladosti on Friday (27 Dec). Novi Sad City Assembly session postponed after students blocked a central intersection and paid tribute to victims (26 Dec).
- FDU students added 15 more names to their list of attackers (per commentary, demand "partly met"); government has "partly" published documentation.
- 26 Dec: Students stated "no demand met" and published a detailed explanation of demand one. Missing per Faculty of Civil Engineering/Architects' Association: contracts with contractors and supervision, who did what and at what cost, why reconstruction cost rose "five times," who is responsible for two ceremonial openings without a use permit (students' claims). Government and Infrastruktura železnice say contracts and site records are held by contractor/supervisor or seized by prosecution and not in public electronic records.

**Government "demands fulfilled" campaign (condensed):** Vučić presented documents 11–13 Dec (195 documents; page counts conflict); annex raised Novi Sad–Kelebija costs by about $87m; Infrastruktura železnice added 376 documents (19 Dec); Government (20 Dec) says everything possible published. Canopy repair price in annex about $29,000. Education Minister (23 Dec) offered talks, called Slavija a political plan. Information Commissioner unsure of lawfulness of presidential display (18 Dec).

**Watch:** Whether students meet Dolovac and outcome; prosecution action on documentation/attackers; BIA contact; Vučić's Sava Centar event; Niš bridge blockade (27 Dec); further uploads; ex-director's statements; evidence for "13 prosecuted"; 20 Jan classes; Vesić delegation liability.

**Verify:** Arrest/prosecution figures; document counts; missing contracts; "five times" cost claim; permit status; attackers' identities; BIA incident; $87m and $29,000 context.
T1.summary_briefed:
**Story: Reconstruction documentation (Serbia, from November 2024). Status as of 2024-12-27**

**Context:** On 1 Nov 2024 the Novi Sad station canopy collapsed, killing 15. Students blockading faculties demand, among other things, publication of the complete reconstruction documentation. Blockades continue across Belgrade, Novi Sad, Kragujevac and Niš (50+ faculties reported, plus secondary schools). The 22 Dec Slavija gathering was described as the largest in Serbia this century. Silences for the 15 victims continue. On 25–26 Dec students blocked a Novi Sad intersection (the city assembly session was postponed) and announced a blockade of the Niš Most mladosti on Friday; Niš University said it backs the demands but opposes blocking faculties. A secondary-school collective said the blockade will continue after 20 Jan 2025 if its conditions are not met.

**P1 (all documentation published): affirmed by government and SNS-aligned actors; contested as incomplete by students, opposition, professional bodies, a watchdog NGO and commentators. The dispute is unchanged in this period; the new material is student-side.**

**Publication facts (reported):** The government site posted 128 documents on 12 Dec and 22 more on 13 Dec. Government and president counted 195 documents, over 4,000 pages; the Ministry of Finance cited "over 40,000 pages". On 19 Dec Infrastruktura železnice reportedly published 376 additional documents, stating that subcontractor contracts and site documentation are held by the contractor and the professional supervision body. On 20 Dec the Government said the Agency for Business Registers had submitted complete CEOP records (cut-off 12 Dec). A published annex to the commercial contract reportedly shows about $29,000 for canopy repair.

**Affirming or hedging (government side):**
- **president (11–14 Dec):** All 195 documents published, same as the prosecution holds; student demands "fully met".
- **speaker (13, 16, 18 Dec):** Documentation published and "never secret"; demands met.
- **pm_vucevic (13–20 Dec):** All documents published; topic "finished" (16 Dec). On 20 Dec: demands met, new documentation being supplemented, "everything we can will be published".
- **ministry_finance (16 Dec):** All demands met, over 40,000 pages.
- **government_vucevic (20 Dec):** "Published everything that could be"; documentation physically seized by the prosecution in original is unavailable; publication continues. This qualified earlier unqualified claims.
- **ministry_education (23 Dec):** Students demanded publication "and they got that"; unqualified.
- Coverage (26 Dec) restates the government's position as: everything possible was published, and the missing documents are those physically seized by the prosecution and not covered by public electronic records.

**Contesting P1:**
- **academic:Faculty of Civil Engineering Belgrade (19 Dec):** Preliminary analysis found missing design documentation, contract documentation (subcontractor contracts and annexes) and site documentation (construction logs, payment statements, inspection book, certificates, geodetic survey, declarations).
- **students_blockade (13–26 Dec):** No demand fully met. On 26 Dec students stated the documentation is published in incomplete form, with key parts missing such as contracts with contractors and supervisors, which prevents full analysis of possible failures. They said technical faculties and the architects' association found key documentation still missing for establishing criminal responsibility. Specifically missing, they say: who did what and at what cost, why the price rose five-fold, and who is responsible for the station being ceremonially opened twice without a use permit. They also published a detailed explanation of the first demand, describing the documentation as currently unavailable to the public.
- **party_ssp (23, 25 Dec):** A vice-president (23 Dec) said young people want complete documentation published. On 25 Dec the SSP president said the opposition must jointly insist that all documentation be made public, and claimed (opinion) that the president would find this hard because the scale of corruption would be seen.
- **Commentators/professors (21–26 Dec):** Opinions that missing financial documentation is key, that authorities cannot meet the demand because of potential criminal exposure, and (26 Dec) that students seek full publication to expose routes of corruption, including which firms won tenders. All unverified.
- **Other contesters:** [person]'s "Solidarnost" (21 Dec); ngo:Transparentnost Srbija (financing and contracting documents missing); ngo:Udruženje arhitekata Srbije (18 Dec, technical documentation incomplete); experts, party_nps and opposition_unspecified (secret contracts, tenders, payment records missing).
- **Partial characterisation (25 Dec):** One outlet described the Government as having "partially" published the documentation (attributed to the outlet, not an actor).
- **institution:Poverenik (18 Dec):** Cannot say whether the president's display was lawful.

**Prosecution track:** On 25 Dec law students delivered about 1,000 letters to the Republic Public Prosecutor's Office (prosecution_republic) asking the Republic Public Prosecutor to do her job under the law and begin meeting the student demands. She accepted the letter and invited students to talk; students chanted "no negotiations". A 24 Dec legal commentary said she has authority to inspect all documentation covered by the demand; no action reported.

**Other:** On 25 Dec reports said BIA invited a student to a "friendly conversation" at the police, the first reported BIA contact with blockading students.

**Open points:** whether the "seized by prosecution" exclusion covers the items the faculty lists; whether the Republic Public Prosecutor will act on the invitation or on the documentation; whether government will announce an end to publication.

**Status as of 2024-12-26/27: The standoff continues but the tone from the top has shifted. Vučić (RTS, 26 Dec) praised the students, said he "accepted all demands," and told them to "find a way to end it with their victory," while still rejecting a transitional government. Other SNS officials keep the hardline "opposition power grab" framing. Students, plenums, professors, unions and opposition say no demand is fully met. Blockades continue (63+ faculties at five state universities, plus private faculties, vocational schools and now many high schools).**

**Background:** On 1 Nov 2024 the reconstructed Novi Sadu station canopy collapsed, killing 15. [person] resigned; about a dozen officials/designers were arrested, then released. [person] told prosecutors Vesić ran the project and had arranged it with Vučić. [person] speculates an indictment may come quickly as a show of compliance.

**Student demands:** publish full station-reconstruction documentation; drop charges against detained students/activists/citizens; file criminal complaints against all attackers of students, professors and citizens; raise faculty budgets 20%. On 26 Dec students published a detailed list of missing documentation ("first demand not fulfilled").

**Government position:**
- Vučić: said he accepted the demands, but fully meeting them would cost an extra €260m and "nobody can fulfil them to the end." Said the demands are now directed at the prosecution and praised students for not adding political demands such as a transitional government ("nonsense" wanted by parties that can't clear 6–7%). Announced the "fiercest anti-corruption fight" by 31 Mar and a new movement from mid-March. Noted many faculties plan exam terms and urged students to find a way to finish "with their victory."
- Vučević: all demands met; "no transitional government… never a mandate without elections." Says many students don't protest, and the government backs SKONUS and other "legal" organizations' call to allow exams. Other SNS figures (Jovanov, Đukanović, Glišić) claim the opposition seeks power without elections, via violence on the 5 Oct 2000 model or pressure for a transitional government, and accuse it of threats and intimidation. Pro-government media attack Ješić (he said the goal is Vučić's removal and spoke of "chaos") and celebrities backing protests. Analyst Klačar: a transitional government requires prior government–opposition agreement, which is absent; the only precedent was 2000.
- Education ministry: winter break advanced; inspectors threatened for schools.

**Prosecution:** On 25 Dec ~1,000 identical letters were delivered to Supreme Public Prosecutor Zagorka Dolovac after a march (15 minutes' silence in front of the Government). She invited students to talk; students said they cannot form a delegation yet and will decide after faculty plenums ("no negotiations" chants). Law professor Pajtić says no meeting is needed.

**Mobilization:** A student tried to enter an SNS youth forum at Sava Centar where Vučić and Vučević were expected. Novi Sad students blocked an intersection near Promenada and the city assembly session was postponed. Belgrade city assembly session was tense, with hooded men pushing activists and councillors, and the budget was passed. Chemistry students report intimidating calls to some colleagues. Jovina gimnazija seniors continue blockade through holidays, alleging sabotage by local authorities. Lawyers are discussing a possible work stoppage in support (Vojvodina Bar's Beljanski confirms discussion). Post workers struck and protested with student support; Lasta bus-company dispute partly resolved.

**Opposition:** PSG (Grbović, Movsesijan) pushes a transitional government (non-party PM, parties, civil society, students by their choice). Ponoš, Ješić, [person] support the idea. Đilas (SSP): synchronized opposition, insist on the demands and document publication; early elections "not the topic now." Nestorović: not time for transitional government talk; opposition must support without usurping. Students (Chemistry) say a transitional government is up to those competent, and they only voice dissatisfaction.

**Analysts:** Spaić, Pajtić and Manojlović argue the demands can't be met without undermining Vučić's system.

**Open questions:** Document verification; prosecutions and the Vesić–Vučić link; whether students meet Dolovac; general strike or lawyers' strike; exam period; school inspections; government escalation; international reaction.

**Confidence:** Moderate; sources are highly partisan and heavily duplicated.

Students in Novi Sad blocked an intersection (26 Dec). Jovina Gimnazija seniors said they will continue the blockade through the holidays. Earlier FDU students' expansion (sanction attackers, remove them from public office) remains the one student-side addition. Students' published specification elaborates the original four rather than adding new ones.

T1.summary_briefed:
**Story: Reconstruction documentation (Serbia, from November 2024). Status as of 2025-02-21**

**Context:** On 1 Nov 2024 the Novi Sad station canopy collapsed, killing 15. Students in blockade demand: publication of the complete reconstruction documentation; dropping charges against detained students, activists and citizens; prosecution of those who attacked protesters; a 20% higher-education budget increase. Past actions: general strike 24 Jan, Autokomanda blockade 27–28 Jan, 27-hour Freedom Bridge blockade 1–2 Feb. pm_vucevic resigned 28 Jan. Faculty, rectorate and school blockades continue; student relay run from Novi Sad reached Belgrade 9–10 Feb; a student march to Kragujevac set out 11 Feb; on 14 Feb secondary-school pupils and citizens reached Trg Republike. On 6 Feb the Belgrade University Senate formed two expert working groups to assess whether the demands are met. Protests, silent gatherings and tributes continued 17–20 Feb in several cities. "Kultura u blokadi" (18 Feb) demanded "complete documentation" on the EXPO 2027 project (separate from the station case).

**P1 (all documentation published): contested.** Stances by actor:

- **president:** on 27 Jan said all demands were met and the whole documentation is published. On 6 Feb said "we gave everything we have"; asked how anyone could say whether it is complete; invited students to talk to prosecutors. On 4 Feb invited professors and university representatives to talks; the rectors' collegium declined.
- **pm_vucevic:** on 1 Feb said the prosecution published all documentation, "several thousand documents on tens of thousands of pages". On 5 Feb said "almost 99 percent" of what was requested is published; the remainder "physically and legally does not exist".
- **Government (letter to EU-member embassies, reported 10–12 Feb):** says it fulfilled all student demands. On documentation it states at least 559 links with 13,042 documents, plus 925 more ready for publication, and that some documents "are not yet in the state's possession". This differs from the earlier "all published" wording, implying some material is unpublished or not held. Reactions (11 Feb): a sociologist said that those who repeatedly publish documentation while each time claiming completeness are recognised as liars; an opposition figure (party unspecified) said documentation on Chinese investors and actual payments is missing.
- **ministry_construction (2 Feb):** published "all requested and available" documentation on the Belgrade–Subotica–Kelebija project; invited the Faculty to inspect originals.
- **prosecution_ns_higher:** says it published all evidentiary documentation it holds (791 items; victim medical material excluded); 13 accused. On 3 Feb it opened a corruption investigation into the reconstruction; its anti-corruption unit and police were checking authenticity of published documents and firms' finances. On 12–13 Feb it said the indictment is expected soon to become legally effective and the first main hearing should be public.
- **prosecution_republic (30 Jan):** said the first demand is fulfilled by "complete documentation" on the Novi Sad prosecution site.
- **prosecution_organised_crime (12 Feb):** a team formed 12 Dec analyses "all documentation" on financial flows published by the Novi Sad prosecution, the Government and the railway infrastructure company, plus material supplied on request. This describes what it analyses, not whether publication is complete. A lawyer (16 Feb) called a recent delegation of a prosecutor an initiative from the top of government meant to protect corrupt interests; his assessment.
- **Pro-government commentary:** says professors dismiss the published documentation and keep up "fog"; calls the inquiry committee political.
- **students_blockade:** none of the demands fully met (reaffirmed 11, 14, 17 Feb). On 9 Feb a student said they were told three times all was published and more kept turning up; about 20,000 documents on three sites are hard to navigate. On 18 Feb a student said publication shows institutions starting to do their duty (partial acknowledgment, not a claim of completeness). A 20 Feb analysis described the demand as insistence on publishing the "complete documentation" and on the flow of money in the reconstruction.
- **academic:Faculty of Civil Engineering Belgrade:** has repeatedly published analyses listing missing or incomplete papers.
- **Inquiry committee (formed 5 Feb):** a civil-engineer member said key elements (new contract, annex 4, accompanying papers) are "still not fully available". On 19 Feb the committee called for all documentation on EXPO facility construction to be published publicly "as soon as possible, without delay", and urged withdrawal of the EXPO special law.
- **European Parliament (reported 20 Feb via a Serbian official):** MEPs are interested in state bodies' accountability; the official said students expect answers on whether all documentation is available and whether proceedings have been launched against those responsible. This is the official's account of their interest, not an EP position.
- **party_ds (18 Feb):** framed publication as an open question.
- **Other voices:** an analyst (19 Feb) predicted the authorities may offer new "concessions", such as publishing further documentation, with no way to know whether something is missing again. SKC student blockaders (20 Feb) said they will announce deblokade terms only once they see full SKC documentation (separate issue).

**Status as of 2025-02-21: Higher-education talks have produced an agreed draft law, which the University of Belgrade rectors' collegium calls a "significant step" and the government calls fulfillment of the fourth demand. Students have not confirmed this. The government/ProGlas dispute over a transitional government continues; Vučić still rules out both a transitional government and snap elections. Students remain in blockade, with a 1 March mobilization in preparation. PM Vučević resigned 28 Jan and remains caretaker.**

**Background:** On 1 Nov 2024 the Novi Sad station canopy collapsed, killing 15. [person] resigned. A 13-person indictment (late Dec) is called a "farce" by the opposition. Civil Engineering Faculty analyses list missing documents; the government says 20,000 documents were published.

**Student demands:** publish full documentation; drop charges against detained protesters; prosecute attackers; raise the higher-education budget 20% (later supplemented with state coverage of 50% of tuition). Novi Sad adds resignations of Vučević and the mayor. 60+ faculties are blockaded; teachers and high-school students have joined.

**Recent events:**
- **15 Feb:** Vučić, in Sremska Mitrovica, said there would be no transitional government. "While I am president" there would be a Serbian government elected by the Assembly with at least 50% new ministers, and a new movement from 15 March. Students blockaded Kragujevac; the cause of a possible stampede there is still unexplained.
- **17 Feb:** ProGlas proposed a 3–10 month transitional government under five principles. Opposition figures (Aleksić, Srbija centar) endorsed it. Vučić and SNS dismissed it as a "colored revolution" and insisted that power comes only through elections.
- **19–20 Feb, transitional-government rift:** ProGlas founder [person] said ProGlas did not coordinate with opposition parties (nor they with it), calling the system "captured" and the transitional government useful. Pro-government outlets spin her remarks as admitting an opposition power struggle, and the full context of her remarks is unverified. Other opposition voices (NADA/Mihailović) want all demands merged into one and elections run by a neutral authority. [person] favors direct pressure on Vučić over a transitional government. Pro-government figures (Glišić) call the transitional government a "closed topic" and say demands 1–3 are met and only the "added" demand remains.
- **Fourth demand (18–20 Feb):** After three days of talks with the education and finance ministries and other state universities, the Education Ministry said it would send the government amendments to the Higher Education Law "to realize the state's positive answer." The extended rectors' collegium of UB said the text is "essentially in line" with its principles and draft law (including state coverage of 50% of tuition), calling it an "important step" that also meets UB's longstanding requests, and said the final agreed version goes to the adoption procedure. Whether the student plenums accept this is not yet reported. Finance Minister Mali had earlier said 12.01bn dinars were already secured. Vučić claims professors are satisfied but cannot say so because of the plenums, an assertion that is unverified.
- **Polling:** Crta says nearly 60% of citizens trust students and 52% say demands are not fulfilled (Crta is an advocacy organization).
- **Schools/labor:** The Education Ministry says 8% of schools are in blockade, while earlier reporting cited 400+ in some stoppage (figures conflict). Teachers announce a new five-day work stoppage. Protests continue by GSP Belgrade workers (joined by students), Pošta Srbije workers in Novi Sad, farmers in Rača, and "Zastani, Srbijo" gatherings. Culture workers blockaded the Kulturni centar Beograda hall (18 Feb), which the KCB collective has commented on.
- **EU dimension:** At a European Parliament debate, MEP Anna Marija Vicsek (Hungarian-minority, Fidesz-affiliated) said all student demands are fulfilled. Milivojević says other MEPs disagreed and that OSCE/ODIHR recommendations are unmet. Picula's report was critical.
- **Other:** DeepSeek analysis of the protests is circulating in media (low evidential value). Pro-government media attack Čanak and Jovanović (Novi DSS), alleging planned airport or media blockades, which are unverified.

**Open questions:** Will students endorse or reject the law as fulfilling the fourth demand, and will it pass? Will the transitional-government split deepen, and will students take a position? Will elections be called? What will the 1 March mobilization look like? Cause of the Kragujevac stampede? EU posture?

**Confidence:** Moderate; sources heavily partisan and duplicated.

T1.summary_unbriefed:
**Story: Reconstruction documentation (Serbia, from November 2024), status as of 2025-03-23**

**Background:** On 1 Nov 2024 the canopy at the Novi Sad railway station collapsed. The death toll was originally 15; student and media coverage on 21 Mar now cites 16 dead (apparently a later death; not confirmed in the excerpts). The station was rebuilt in phases within the Belgrade–Budapest rail project with China and Hungary. Core dispute: who is responsible, and whether the canopy fell within the reconstruction documentation. CIP documents of 15 Nov showed canopy work planned, contradicting Tica's 1 Nov "not in scope" claim. Vučić first said no work was done on the canopy, then "some coating"; his claims that all documentation was published proved repeatedly untrue. Vučević resigned as PM after the 29 Jan attack on students by SNS supporters, de facto toppling the government (a transitional government is in place).

**15 Mar mass protest:** Student blockaders called a large protest in Belgrade. BBC called it probably one of the largest in Serbian history. Protests have lasted over four months. Sound-cannon allegations followed; the Council of Europe responded on 20 Mar (nature and strength not visible).

**Sound-cannon track (new, 21 Mar):** [person] says prosecutors must establish who ordered use of the sound weapon, temporarily seize all MUP sound cannons, order expert examination, and collect medical records (hundreds of injured reportedly sought medical care). SSP MP [person] published official documents showing MUP sought 16 sound cannons (seven 450XL, the type suspected of being used, and nine type 100). Reports say MUP paid the intermediary "Romax" about three times what the US side paid the manufacturer directly. The authorities first denied having the devices, later admitted having them, and still claim they were not used that day. All of this is partisan or unverified.

**Students' four demands:** (1) publish complete reconstruction documentation; (2) identify and prosecute all attackers of students, professors and citizens; drop charges against detained protesters; (3) criminal complaints against attackers (per the earlier list); (4) raise university funding by 20%. Official framing: documentation published repeatedly, 13 detainees pardoned, proceedings opened against attackers, Law on Higher Education amended. Finance Minister Siniša Mali said an additional RSD 12.01bn was secured for higher education. Students say demands remain unmet. Anonymous professor's letters: the fifth (15 Mar) maps responsibility to prosecutors and the Government. **New (22 Mar):** the sixth letter ("four lessons from North Macedonia") contrasts the Kočani nightclub case, where all documentation reached prosecutors the same day (16 Mar) and political responsibility followed promptly, with Serbia, where parts of the site logs and other documents showing responsibility are missing.

**Political track:** On 20 Mar the opposition offered an agreement on a "Government of National Trust". It assumes no change to the current ministry structure and sets minimum conditions for free elections, including urgent publication of the complete canopy documentation and no executive pressure on the judiciary. Signatories and status not visible.

**Pressure on higher education and other sectors (new/ongoing):** Inspection oversight of faculties is under way (21 Mar); critics read it as pressure, with FDU dean [person] saying he is ready and has nothing to hide. Belgrade museums and cultural institutions struck 17–19 Mar. Parents have filed three-digit numbers of constitutional appeals over denied schooling. Novi Sad deans put 11 questions to authorities. On 21 Mar Novi Sad citizens walked in silence to honour Vukašin and other victims; students bid Vukašin farewell; protests also occurred in Niš, and SNS held a party meeting. Politico (17 Mar): Vučić is under pressure but his fall is "far off".

**Investigation:**
- **Novi Sad VJT:** indicted 13 on 30 Dec (Art. 288 para 2); Higher Court confirmation pending. Ex-minister Vesić defends himself from liberty; a corruption investigation opened 3 Feb.
- **New (21 Mar):** the VJT-published documentation includes an email inviting [person], on Vesić's behalf, to the station's opening. It is dated 5 June rather than 5 July, when the event took place, which may be an error. The Infrastructure of Railways manager says Vesić invited her by phone message.
- **JTOK:** took over financial-flows proceedings (12 Feb); critics see delay.
- **Belgrade VJT Special Anti-Corruption Department:** indicted three on 4 Mar; the case against two others was dropped.
- **EPPO (14 Mar):** reportedly investigating; scope unconfirmed.
- Unverified: Milićević's claims of a later documentation supplement; an expert's alternative cause theory; Utiber denies supervisory responsibility.

**Corruption indicators (partisan or unverified):** Đajić alleges forged site logs and cost growth from €3.1m to €16m, naming Vesić, Kojić and Vukšić. Nearly 200 subcontractors; Starting paid at least €5.1m via eight annexes. Dašić estimates the Novi Sad–Subotica section at 2–2.5x realistic per-km cost. Forbes: Chinese firms complained of unpaid €65m. The station cost reportedly rose almost threefold.

**Documentation completeness:** Government claims 559 links and 13,042 documents. The University of Belgrade expert group found gaps: subcontractor/supplier selection documents, investor consents, subcontracts with annexes, and statements and invoices.

**Open items:** Higher Court confirmation; EPPO scope; fate of the opposition's propos

**Status as of 2025-03-22: Government-formation deadlock persists, with Vučić now publicly refusing any "transitional" (opposition-shaped) government while teasing his own new movement. The state-versus-university conflict has escalated over funding and inspections, and tension around incidents in Niš is rising. Blockades, strikes and the sound-cannon dispute continue.**

**Background:** The 1 Nov 2024 Novi Sad station canopy collapse killed 15 (some outlets now say 16). Vesić resigned and a 13-person indictment followed, which the opposition calls a "farce." Vučević resigned on 28 Jan. 60+ faculties are blockaded, and a 7 March general strike drew large crowds. The 15 March Belgrade protest was called the largest in Serbia's history; a panic occurred during the 15 minutes of silence, and opposition and students allege a banned "sound cannon" was used (Vučić denies use; Brnabić says nobody saw or heard it).

**Government formation:**
- The Assembly noted Vučević's resignation on 19 March, starting the deadline clock. If no government is formed, elections are likely around 8 June.
- Parliamentary opposition (NPS, ZLF, SSP, PSG, Srbija centar, New DSS, POKS) proposed a "government of national trust" on 20-21 March, with a non-party PM, about nine months in office, and the opposition naming the PM and eight key ministries. DS declined to take part, and Nestorović's group and Pavlović's group did not back it. Critics (e.g. Prof. Radonjić) say a government including the authorities cannot be "national trust." Students have said an expert government is not their responsibility, and pro-government voices (Antić) claim students never backed it.
- On 22 March Vučić said, on the "Đilas government": "I won't participate; let Schieder and the others choose it; citizens of Serbia will decide." This responds to a letter by 31 MEPs urging von der Leyen to say a transitional government is needed. He will meet von der Leyen in Brussels on Tuesday (25 March). He earlier said it could only happen if SNS does not listen to him, an ambiguous hint, and has said he would never allow it "over his dead body." He also announced a new movement, with an initiative committee, name, programme and symbols to be revealed on 23 March, and said "a call is coming soon," apparently meaning dialogue and an offer to the students, whom he accuses of turning demands into ultimatums.
- Other voices: Abazović (URA) says elections are needed; Popović says public pressure means the ruling coalition no longer decides alone; Brnabić calls the proposal "Đilas's government"; Đurđev and Jeremić call it a hostage-taking or pressure tactic. SPS's Tončev floated Vučić as premier of an election-preparing government.

**Universities vs. state:**
- The Education Ministry ([person]) demanded data on whether classes and exams are being held, and on whether police were notified and disciplinary action taken against blockading students and striking staff. It announced extraordinary inspections of Belgrade University faculties, and warned of "red lines." The Ministry denied inviting police onto campuses.
- The University of Belgrade rejected "serving as an instrument of pressure," reaffirmed support for the student demands, and formed a legal team. It warned that withholding salary funds would be illegal conditioning, and cited hate speech and a media lynching of the rector. Students say the "humiliation of the academic community will not go unpunished."
- A criminal complaint was filed against Niš [person], and another against a Kragujevac rector.

**Niš incident (21 March):** Protesters pelted SNS members with eggs, and Vulin and Brnabić denounced the "lynching" of the Niš mayor. Vučić said he was shocked that the "main aggressor" was freed and the prosecutor did not seek detention. Niš citizen protests continue.

**Other fronts:**
- Student blockades continue (GSP Sava depot blocked; "Nismo vaše mete" protest near the London café). Teachers hold daily 16-minute silences (Kraljevo), high-schoolers marched in Sremska Mitrovica, and Novi Sad held a silent walk.
- Pionirski Park: the "students who want to study" group says it stays until its demands are met. Srbija centar demands dismissal of Obrenovac officials who were in the park on 15 March, alleging that people with criminal records were brought in.
- The Engineers Chamber got an interim board, which the "Zahtevi inženjera" group welcomed as meeting a key demand.
- RTV Vojvodina: Šper's hunger strike status is unconfirmed in these excerpts.

**Open questions:** Whether SNS forms a "continuity" government or calls elections; the content of Vučić's new movement and his promised "call"; the 25 March von der Leyen meeting; the university funding and inspection clash; the sound-cannon investigation; Niš prosecutions; the 28 March SNS rally.

**Confidence:** Moderate; the sources are heavily partisan and duplicative.

**Summary (as of 23 March 2025): The "sound cannon" incident, Belgrade, 15 March**

**Background:** The "15 for 15" student protest in Belgrade on 15 March 2025 was part of the anti-government movement that began after the November 2024 Novi Sad canopy collapse. Crowd estimates reach about 400,000. At about 19:10, during the 15-minute silence for the victims, a loud, frightening sound sent crowds fleeing near Kralja Milana/Slavija. Students ended the protest about two hours early. Protests continue. PM Vučević has resigned (now "in resignation"), and caretaker-government/election talk continues. Vučić says he expects universities to resume work in April.

**Core dispute: was an LRAD-type "sound cannon" (or vortex/other device) used?**

*Claims that it was:*
- Witnesses describe a fast-approaching sound, nausea, headaches, hearing problems and stampede injuries. [person] says the symptoms suggest a very high-frequency source. Several people say they were turned away or ridiculed at hospitals. Military analyst Radić says a US-type long-range acoustic device was on a Gendarmerie vehicle; [person] says he was present and it was a sound cannon.
- Tepić presented procurement documents showing MUP sought 16 LRADs (7 × 450XL, 9 × 100X, about 81 million dinars) and a photo of a mounted device behind the Assembly. Aleksić says the devices are held by Gendarmerie, SAJ and Belgrade police units.
- **New (21 March):** A criminal complaint was filed with the organised crime prosecutor's office alleging terrorism by Vučić. Complainants cite symptoms (disorientation, dizziness, nausea, heart problems, a sensation of heat) and note that sound cannons are not an authorised coercive means under the Police Law. [person] says prosecutors must establish who bought, ordered and used the weapon. Valjevo graduates filed complaints, including over the stampede and against Informer's Vukelić for spreading panic. Manojlović (Kreni-promeni) launched a petition seeking UN/CoE/OSCE involvement. Ex-Romanian chief military prosecutor Pitu told DW the effects fit "psychological warfare" sound technology used in Romania in 1989. The Guardian reported "growing pressure on Vučić." Abazović (Montenegro's URA) said whoever used the device must go to prison.
- Earlier complaints (SSP, NPS), BCBP/Šabić calls, and EP (Picula) and PACE rapporteur statements stand. BIRN recalled earlier police use of sound weapons against migrants near Sombor.

*Official position:*
- Dačić admits MUP owns LRAD 100X/450XL (bought 2021), says they are used only for voice warnings, were not used on 15 March, and that the vehicle stayed stationary and no sound was played except during preparations/exercises. He denies owning a "vortex" device. **New:** acting police director Vasiljević said all police units sent reports to the prosecution stating that no MUP officer or other security-service member used such a means, and that police remain available for any further requests. On 22 March MUP again denied the claims, citing the First Basic Prosecutor's statement that "unambiguously" nobody on duty heard, saw or used a sound cannon, and Genasys's statement that the recordings do not support LRAD use.
- Genasys (19–20 March) said the recordings reviewed don't support LRAD use; caveat: it addressed recordings, not the vehicle or MUP's use, and is a commercial party. NASA-linked analyst Matman said the videos don't suggest a sonic weapon.
- **Vučić (21 March):** says the opposition lied "brutally" because its "revolution failed"; repeated that he is "no longer president" if one proof appears; claimed MUP, BIA and the manufacturer all deny use, that the army said it has only anti-drone guns, and that EU states use stronger devices routinely. Vučević earlier asked for FBI/FSB/US investigators. Brnabić mocks shifting opposition theories (sound cannon, electromagnetic, vortex). Pro-government media claim a Canadian influencer was paid $6,000 to push the claim (unverified). Pilja rejected the PACE rapporteurs' statement as unbalanced; Serbia's CoE mission calls the claims a lie. Higher Prosecutor's earlier order to identify people spreading "false information" is read by critics as intimidation. Vulin and Glišić attack Abazović.

**State of evidence:** No independent technical or forensic confirmation of use has emerged, and the prosecution's inquiry relies on police self-reports. MUP's admitted LRAD ownership, the vehicle photo and shifting denials sustain suspicion; the manufacturer's statement is the government's main exoneration. The cause of the sound and stampede remains unexplained.

**Watch for:** prosecutors' actions on the complaints and police reports; whether FBI/FSB/US investigators engage; EU/PACE/UN response; independent audio/forensic analysis; the vehicle-mounted device question; prosecutions over "false information"; election developments.

**Story: Crowd sizes, 15 March and 12 April (Serbia, from November 2024)**
*Status as of excerpts through 2025-03-23. Still nothing on 12 April itself; Vučić's mid-April reference remains the only forward-looking item.*

**Context:** Anti-government protests, student-led, have run since the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station collapse. A 16th victim (19-year-old Vukašin C.) died at VMA on 21 March; about 10,000 marched in a commemorative walk in Novi Sad. The 15 March Belgrade rally was a major test, and attendance is politically contested. Sources mix pro-government outlets (Informer/Alo-style, Tanjug, official statements) with independent/opposition-leaning media (Nova, N1, Danas) and foreign press.

**Official figures for 15 March:**
- MUP: about 107,000 at the peak, across all Belgrade locations. Vučić cited a military estimate of 88,000, police 107,000, and BIA in between; on 18 March he said it was "less than 107,000 but more than 88,000," blaming BIA double-counting. Government figures are routinely quoted against opposition ones.
- Brnabić's "1.68 million" (20 March) was sarcasm, not a figure.
- New: a US outlet (per Vučić's 22 March interview coverage) summarized turnout as "between 107,000 and 325,000 depending on estimates," i.e., foreign press now frames it as the official-to-AJS range. Vučić claimed protesters destroyed 186 tractors and that the only big fight was among themselves.

**Independent and external estimates:**
- AJS: 275,000–325,000, "possibly more." Evropska pravda: 275,000–315,000, a country record. Frankfurter Rundschau ~300,000; Mediapart 275,000–375,000; Politico ~300,000 (noting the old people-per-area method is unreliable here).
- Higher claims: Đilas "half a million"; the far-right Otadžbina (22 March) said "more than half a million," the "largest rally in Serbia's history" (a notable claim from an anti-Vučić but non-liberal source, still unsourced). Josipa Lisac-related coverage (21 March) mentions "even a million" in circulation as an estimate still being assessed. The fake-Mossad "one million" claim is non-credible. [person]'s op-ed uses "260,000" young people (a rhetorical or unsourced figure, apparently student-related).
- **Council of Europe PACE rapporteurs (20 March):** "at least 100,000," a cautious floor and the first institutional international statement.
- Transparency Serbia's request for MUP's method (peak vs cumulative; 210,000 for the 2023 rally vs 107,000 now) remains unanswered.

**Sound-cannon allegation (linked):**
- The Kreni-Promeni petition to UN special rapporteurs and the Council of Europe passed 590,000 signatures by Thursday 20 March (the Guardian, via Serbian coverage: "growing pressure on Vučić"), calling for an independent international investigation. The CoE rapporteurs expressed "deep concern."
- The government denies it (Vučić, Brnabić, BIA, army). Nothing is independently verified.

**New developments, 21–22 March:**
- Protesters blocked GSP (Belgrade public transport) depots on 21 March. PM Vučević claimed 400,000 users were affected and "20 people punished 400,000 citizens"; SNS's Mirković cited 16 bus and 10 tram lines and 280 vehicles. Pro-government messaging now stresses disruption to citizens. Vučević and Brnabić skipped an SNS rally in Niš, citing security, where residents reportedly pelted SNS members with eggs.
- Vučić (22 March, Leskovac): "never giving up my policy"; protesters' politics is "violence." Other government voices (Đurić) say organizers' radicalization is eroding dialogue. Vučić's new movement and the "15 April" end date are still unexplained.

**Key analytic points:**
- The gap persists: government 88k–107k vs independent 275k–375k, with the CoE 100k floor and a growing foreign-press convention of citing both. Pro-government rhetoric is shifting from crowd size to disruption and violence.
- Incentives: government minimizes; organizers and some opposition maximize. AJS methodology still lacks independent review in the excerpts.

**Still needed:** AJS methodology details, MUP's reply to Transparency Serbia, independent counts, and any coverage of 12 April (planning, expected turnout, official or AJS counts).

**Story: Reconstruction documentation (Serbia, from November 2024), status as of 2025-04-30**

**Background:** On 1 Nov 2024 the canopy at the Novi Sad railway station collapsed. Early reports gave 15 dead; sources now cite 16 dead plus one person critically injured. The station was rebuilt in phases within the Belgrade–Budapest rail project with China and Hungary. Core dispute: who is responsible, and whether the canopy fell within the reconstruction documentation. CIP documents of 15 Nov showed canopy work planned, contradicting Tica's 1 Nov "not in scope" claim. Vučić first said no work was done on the canopy, then "some coating"; his claims that all documentation was published proved repeatedly untrue. Vučević resigned as PM after the 29 Jan attack on students, toppling the government (a government in resignation/transition remains). Publication of the complete documentation remains a core student demand and the basis of the university blockades.

**Prosecution case:**
- **First indictment confirmed (17 Apr).** Three defendants (names and roles not captured; likely technical-inspection commission members, unconfirmed). Charges concern the technical-acceptance function: they allegedly did not establish that conditions for a use permit were met, did not check this during trial operation, and filed no report to the investor, contrary to the Law on Planning and Construction. They allegedly did not verify completeness of technical documentation (no works notification, no conformity check against the designed structure, no check of key structural elements, construction logs or control samples, no follow-up testing of the canopy in front of vestibule "B"), and issued technical-inspection reports despite no assessment of the existing building's condition and no preliminary stability investigations. Separate from the Vesić case; whether others will be charged is unclear.
- Novi Sad Higher Public Prosecutor's Office also charges ex-construction minister [person] with knowing the works were unfinished, not reported on time, with no technical inspection or use permit before opening. On 12 Feb Supreme Public Prosecutor Zagorka Dolovac sent files to the Organized Crime Prosecutor's Office for possible corruption offences; prosecutors and financial forensic experts are analysing documentation. No outcome reported. On 24 Mar "Pobunjeni univerzitet" demanded Dolovac's resignation. A 4 Apr opposition-leaning piece speculated that Mihajlović, Vesić and [person] could face scrutiny (no case reported).

**Subcontractor angle:** Starting, a known subcontractor on the Belgrade–Budapest line, reportedly reached about €100 million revenue in 2024. In published documentation it signed three contracts worth about €7 million for the Novi Sad–Hungary reconstruction (one in 2021, two in 2022). Source framing implies scrutiny of subcontractor gains; no wrongdoing alleged. On 24 Apr a report said it has been revealed whom Starting has sued (details not captured); the angle continues to draw media attention.

**Recent threads:**
- **New minister:** [person] is incoming Minister of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure (technocrat; 2012–14 oversaw construction and use permits). In March she declared all technical site documentation published, the same contested claim made by others.
- **Explosives angle (15 Apr):** Police reportedly checked on day one whether explosives caused the collapse. About 100 testimonies contain no questions on explosives, and published documentation has no forensic on-site finding. Feeds the missing-documents argument and possible sabotage theories; unverified.
- **Sound-cannon investigation:** Over 50 complaints from those injured at the 15 Mar protest filed; prosecution summoning them as witnesses and requesting medical records. A 19 Apr analysis suggests a legal route for secrecy around the device.
- **Prosecutorial controversy:** [person]'s decisions criticised; Vučić (11 Apr) threatened a prosecutor who allegedly refused to arrest journalists of "blockader" media.
- **Pošta/transparency angle (20 Apr):** A Post Office worker says she was demoted for supporting students; an unattributed quote demands removal of a "confidential" label placed on documentation by the Supervisory Board. Link to the station case unclear.
- **University/prosecution front (23 Apr):** Pro-government Informer reports that rector [person] declined a meeting with the PM, and that the First Basic Public Prosecutor's Office demanded he urgently submit all decisions made during the blockade and on student protests. Hostile source; signals escalating legal pressure on the student movement, not on the canopy investigation itself.
- **Vučić rhetoric (24 Apr):** He repeated that the documentation was delivered and that critics "haven't said what is missing" (contradicted by experts and the Inquiry Commission), alleged a "colour revolution" with large protest food costs (unverified), said some in Europe voice demands identical to the students', and announced the "biggest military parade" for 15 Sept. Pattern: framing the documentation demand as foreign-backed and politically driven.
- **Electoral framing (25 Apr):** Prof. Cvetičanin (opposition-leaning commentary) argues full publication would show the extent of corruption and predicts a student-backed list would eliminate the ruling SNS. The documentation demand is increasingly tied to a possible electoral list.
- **Opinion (26 Apr):** An opinion piece blames the SNS government for not meeting student demands, suggesting authorities either cannot (documentation missing, unproven) or will not (protecting individuals). Commentary only.
- **NEW (28 Apr) Parliament/REM:** A parliamentary committee voted a new competition for REM council members after a 3.5-hour heated session. Opposition MPs at the outset sharply condemned police use of force against demon

**Story: Crowd sizes, 15 March and 12 April (Serbia, from November 2024)**
*Status as of excerpts through 2025-04-24. The 12 April SNS/government rally "Ne damo Srbiju" remains the reference point, but the dispute is now mostly a recurring rhetorical weapon. Newest coverage (22 April) concerns a petition against a minister's appointment, not a crowd count. No new count of 12 April has appeared.*

**Context:** Student-led anti-government protests have run since the 1 November 2024 Novi Sad railway station collapse (16 dead). The 15 March Belgrade rally is the benchmark. Sources split between pro-government outlets (Informer/Alo/Kurir-style, Tanjug, RTS, officials) and independent or opposition-leaning media (Nova, N1, Danas, Betina reporters) and foreign press.

**12 April rally, claims:**
- **Government line:** Vučić said "145,000" from the stage, citing police first estimates. Brnabić and PM Vučević repeated MUP's 140–150k. Pro-government outlets cite "official MUP data, 145,000" against AJS's "30–40 thousand." Vučić's 13 April reframing (about 126,735–128,080 people entering Belgrade by vehicle) measures arrivals, not simultaneous presence. Claims of "about 300,000 over three days" circulate.
- **Arhiv javnih skupova (AJS):** at least 55,000, the headline figure repeated by BBC, DW, NZZ and AFP. AJS's Nikolić said "no more than 40,000" were present when Vučić began speaking. So 55k (event) and 30–40k (speech moment) are different snapshots; AJS has not published a single reconciled peak. AJS says it has no formal cooperation with any organization and is donation-funded (its own account, no independent review).
- **Opposition figures (unsourced):** Dveri about 50,000; Đilas claims MUP's internal count was about 25,000; Marsenić 45,000; Ejdus about 30,000. None is evidenced.
- **Foreign/analyst framing:** AFP analyst Klačar: beyond the "battle over numbers," energy was weaker than Vučić hoped and the crowd was his loyal base. RFI and NZZ stress organized buses and coercion allegations, plus a large remaining support base.
- **21 April:** SNS Presidency member [person] referred to "700 thousand honest, hardworking people." This is an SNS-aligned supporter or membership figure, not a crowd count and not tied to 12 April. Notable only as another large unsourced figure in circulation.

**15 March benchmark:**
- Official: MUP about 107,000 peak.
- Independent: AJS 275,000–325,000; Guardian about 325,000; Politico/Mediapart 275,000–375,000; RFI "300,000+"; PACE rapporteurs "at least 100,000" floor. AFP/Moscow Times use the range "100,000–300,000." Transparency Serbia's request for MUP's method is unanswered. Unsourced 500k–1M claims aren't counts.
- **20 April (N1-style explainer on Balkan protests):** repeats AJS's 275–325k and stresses the figure is impressive given alleged obstruction (intimidation, suspended intercity departures to Belgrade, suspended Belgrade transit). AJS-sourced framing from an opposition-leaning outlet.
- Earlier: pro-government columnist Bakarec claimed CNN reported "only 100,000" (unverified; resembles the PACE/AFP floor) and used it for a "convincing minority" argument. Population-share arguments are not measurements.

**AJS comparisons and scaling:**
- **Istanbul (20 April):** AJS analyzed the protest over the mayor's arrest (almost 150,000 people on 90,000 m²), equating it proportionally to about 13,500 people in Belgrade. Per-capita normalization, not a Belgrade count.
- **Kraljevo (16 April):** AJS estimated about 15,000, "proportional to 330,000 in Belgrade." Rhetorical scaling, not a Belgrade count. Pro-government outlets accuse AJS of lying and publish rival photos without a figure.

**RTS blockade (no count dispute yet):** By the seventh night (20 April), a Betina reporter claimed "more than 15,000 people" supported students, blockading all entrances and surrounding streets. Single-reporter estimate from a protest-sympathetic outlet; no AJS or police figure reported. Expect the same split pattern.

**Other developments:**
- **22 April:** Dejan [person], a long-time pro-regime analyst, was appointed minister. A petition against his appointment gathered over 18,000 signatures and 45+ civil society organizations in three days. These are petition signatures (not verified here, no independent audit), not crowd counts; anonymous harassment allegations against him circulate in media. Relevant only as another mobilization-size claim.
- Students are lobbying EU institutions (Strasbourg), with a relay-run planned to Brussels before the May European Parliament session. - Each side inflates its own crowds and discounts the other's. AJS (55k) is about 2.6× below the police figure (145k). AJS lacks independent review; MUP discloses no method.
- Snapshot versus arrivals versus multi-day totals are different measures; per-capita scaling, supporter-base figures (700k), petition signatures and population-share arguments are not headcounts.

**Crowd sizes: 15 March and 12 April 2025 (Serbia). Summary as of 24 April 2025.**

*Latest excerpts (22 April) contain no new attendance estimates for either event. They concern a protest and petition over a ministerial appointment (over 18,000 signatories and 45+ civil-society organisations in three days). This is not relevant to P8 or P9, so all positions below are unchanged.*

**P8 – Belgrade protest, 15 March 2025**

*Pre-event context (expectations, not attendance estimates):*
- On 14 March the president said the authorities expected 60,000–80,000 people, about 33,000 from the interior, and that the Archive of Public Gatherings invents figures of 300,000, 500,000 or 1,000,000.
- A party_srce figure said the authorities might later claim 50,000 or 100,000.
- The eve-of-protest gathering (14 March) is a separate event; police estimated about 31,000 at peak.

*Attendance estimates for 15 March:*
- **ministry_interior / police:** about 107,000 at the peak across all Belgrade locations, most from the interior. The acting police director (16 March) called this "very realistic".
- **ministry_defence, as reported by the president:** 88,000.
- **bia, as reported by the president:** between the military and police figures. On 18 March the president said the BIA double-counted people moving between time slots, so the real number was under 107,000 but over 88,000. His 15 March framing was 88,000–107,000.
- **ajs:** 275,000–325,000 (some outlets give 270,000–325,000). Repeated in a 20 April regional-protests overview, which notes the figure is striking given alleged obstruction (intimidation campaign, halted intercity departures, suspended Belgrade public transport). Foreign outlets relay it: about 300,000 (German daily), "about 325,000" with the government disputing it (British daily), 107,000–325,000 depending on estimates (US newspaper), "more than 300,000" (French radio, 14 April).
- **party_ssp:** its leader said on 20 March "half a million" gathered.
- **party:Otadžbina (22 March):** "more than half a million".
- **students_blockade:** one student said estimates above half a million circulate but nobody can know exactly. Individuals and a political consultant (not map actors) cite "a million" or 800,000.
- **speaker (20 March):** sarcastically cited "a million and 680 thousand", apparently mocking high claims; not her own estimate.
- **foreign:Council of Europe rapporteurs (20 March):** "at least 100,000".
- **ngo:Transparentnost Srbija (18 March):** asked police whether their figure is peak or cumulative and what method was used. No reply recorded.
- **Non-map speakers (13–18 April):** a security-studies academic implied roughly 300,000; a professor took "300,000" as a premise; a pro-government column used 107,000 as baseline; an opposition-leaning commentary (15 April) said the government claimed more supporters came on 12 April than attended on 15 March; a Moscow-based English-language outlet (17 April) relayed AFP as "between 100,000 and 300,000"; a pro-government columnist (18 April) attributed a 100,000 figure to "CNN" (unverified, not a map actor's estimate).

*Position of the contest:* Official range 88,000–107,000 versus the Archive's 275,000–325,000, with party_ssp and Otadžbina claiming "half a million". Council of Europe: at least 100,000. Press framings increasingly give a wide range (100,000–300,000). The peak-versus-cumulative method question remains unanswered.

**P9 – Rally "Ne damo Srbiju", Belgrade, 12 April 2025**

*Estimates:*
- **president (12 April):** said during his speech, citing police, that 145,000 were present ("first police estimates"), around 20:20. An AFP report (16 April) noted this alongside the Archive's figure.
- **president (13 April), different figure:** between 126,735 and 128,080 people entered Belgrade, each bus and van video-documented, attributed to police, BIA and the party; more than 120,000 from the interior. This counts entries, not presence. A pro-government column (14 April) repeated "about 128,000". A pro-government outlet (15 April) said the speech was given before "more than 140,000". Per an opposition-side report (14 April), the president said 140–150,000 and that he could bring more.
- **government_vucevic / pm_vucevic (14 April):** the caretaker PM said the official ministry_interior estimate is 145,000, adding that establishing numbers is not the most important thing "but not to be underestimated".
- **speaker (13 April):** ministry_interior estimated 140,000–150,000; she thought there were more.
- **A pro-government outlet (17 April)** repeated 145,000 "according to official ministry_interior data" and said the Archive claimed 30,000–40,000.
- **ajs:** at least 55,000 (count from footage at 19:00, an opening count). On 14 April its representative said that at the start of the president's speech there were no more than 40,000 across the points it could assess, though not all could be measured. He described its method (best moment for SNS rallies is the official start; for student or civic rallies, 30–40 minutes in), said it had no estimate for the simultaneous Novi Pazar gathering, and urged dividing the president's figures for SNS rallies by three and multiplying student ones by three. Foreign coverage (German, French outlets, AFP on 16 April, calling it an "independent counting group") relays about 55,000.
- **party_ssp:** its leader (14 April) said he had information that a ministry_interior estimate put attendance at about 25,000, contradicting the president's 145,000. Unconfirmed; contradicts the figure others attribute to the ministry.
- **party:Dveri (14 April):** about 50,000, calling the rally a fiasco; they put its cost
